manager_rule: Maintain a session-scoped per-cable integer counter 'post_max_escalation_stall[C]' initialized to 0 for each cable index C. After each round R where kelvin_keepout_escalation_count[C] >= 10 (Rule 57 maximum tier, 12x16mm keepout geometry) AND cable C is still counted in kelvin_unrouted OR both /SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO appear in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines': increment post_max_escalation_stall[C] by 1; reset post_max_escalation_stall[C] to 0 immediately whenever cable C's Kelvin gate clears (cable C absent from kelvin_unrouted AND neither member appears in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines'). When post_max_escalation_stall[C] reaches 4: (1) derive the cable-C corridor rectangle as the 12x16mm region centered on the geometric midpoint between cable C's shunt inner-edge pad centroids, identical to the current Rule 56/57 keepout geometry; (2) identify all track segments whose bounding box intersects this corridor rectangle AND whose net is neither /SENSEC{C}_HI nor /SENSEC{C}_LO — these are the competitor tracks to ripup; (3) ripup those competitor segments from the board (remove them, leaving ratlines); do NOT touch segments belonging to /SENSEC{C}_HI or /SENSEC{C}_LO; (4) in round R+1, inject both: (a) the standard Rule 56/57 keepout for cable C at the current escalation tier geometry (12x16mm), AND (b) Kelvin force stubs for /SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO via Rule 33's mandatory_kelvin_bypass protocol per Rule 34 — FR now has both a physically cleared corridor and explicit placement guidance for the Kelvin pair; (5) reset post_max_escalation_stall[C] to 2 immediately after round R+1 is dispatched (retriggers 2 rounds later at stall count 4 again if cable C continues to fail, providing one recovery round before re-clearing); (6) log 'post_max_escalation_corridor_ripup' with fields: (a) round R, (b) cable index C, (c) post_max_escalation_stall count at trigger, (d) list of ripped nets with segment count per net, (e) corridor rectangle geometry (centroid + dimensions), (f) kelvin_unrouted, DRC, and unconnected from round R, (g) whether this is a first-trigger (post_max_escalation_stall reached 4 from 0) or re-trigger (reached 4 from 2). This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 56, and 57; it does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, kelvin_keepout_escalation_count, consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds, or any other session-scoped state maintained by those rules, and does not replace or defer any independent action they mandate. Rationale: Rules 56 and 57 progressively escalate keepout geometry to prevent new routing in the cable-C Kelvin corridor, but keepouts cannot remove tracks FR has already placed there in prior rounds — those competitor tracks are stable, and FR will not voluntarily reroute them even under the maximum 12x16mm constraint. Once kelvin_keepout_escalation_count[C] has reached its ceiling and cable C continues to fail across multiple additional rounds, the corridor contains entrenched competitor tracks that are the proximate cause of the Kelvin stall; keepout-only escalation has demonstrably exhausted its effectiveness. The post-max-escalation ripup is the logical next tier: physically clear the competitor tracks from the corridor, then immediately re-apply the keepout plus Kelvin force stubs so FR can route the Kelvin pair into the now-available space without the same tracks re-entering the corridor in the same round.
